$comment: What a specification must SAY before RTL is generated from it or validated against it. Rules are keyed to section TYPES (any spec with a register map must answer these questions; any spec with a DDR channel must answer those), not to this design — a customised spec is checked by the same rules. Every rule cites the incident that produced it: this file is a ratchet. When validation discovers a gap the hard way, its resolution becomes a rule here so the next spec is checked for it on arrival.

$dispositions.standard: The applicable standard determines the answer. Validation adopts it and files a completion request; checking continues.
$dispositions.decision: A genuine design choice the spec owner must make. Until made, comparisons on the affected field are UNDETERMINED (never pass, never fail).
$dispositions.vocabulary: The spec lacks the words to report a failure class; proposed IDs are used locally and requested upstream.

rules.question: What data accompanies a read of an address the register map does not declare?
rules.consequence: A spec-derived model and a design can both be 'correct' with different answers; the comparison is unfalsifiable until this is stated.
rules.discovered_by: VP_CSR_006 — design returned 0xDEADBEEF, model returned 0; waived as W-001

rules.question: What happens on a write to an undeclared address — error flag, silent drop, or both?
rules.consequence: Error-flag comparison on unmapped writes rests on an assumption.
rules.discovered_by: sibling of VP_CSR_006 (the error flag happened to agree; the spec never said it must)

rules.question: Do byte enables mean anything on a READ, and what value is expected on the request?
rules.consequence: A model predicted full enables on reads; the bus drove none. Neither is wrong.

rules.question: When a status register is read in the same cycle its source changes, does the read return the old or the new value?
rules.consequence: A one-cycle coincidence produced a mismatch that no waiver can express. Registered designs return the old value; the spec must say so.

standard.name: JESD79-3 (DDR3)
standard.note: DM=1 masks the byte. The host-side wishbone sel (1 = write this byte) is the inverse convention.

rules.question: On the DDR channel, does the data-mask pin mask or enable a byte?
rules.consequence: The design drives ~sel (JEDEC-correct); a spec-derived model carried sel through unchanged. The standard decides this one.

rules.question: Does the failure taxonomy have ids for what a queue + arbiter can do wrong — drop a request, invent a command, starve a refresh?
rules.consequence: Checkers reported real defects under locally proposed ids (SCHED_001..003) that the spec cannot name.

rules.question: For every pair of blocks a path connects, what are the port-level signals, widths and handshake between them?
rules.consequence: The drop shipped 11 blocks and no top level; two block pairs did not compose (no bank on cmd_gen's feedback, nothing consuming calibration's ZQCS request). Validation had to author a 75-connection map by hand. Interfaces that are not specified cannot be generated consistently on both sides.
rules.discovered_by: integration_map.json glue entries; fb-bank and ZQCS findings

rules.question: Does the failure taxonomy have an id for violating EVERY timing parameter the timing model states?
rules.consequence: A parameter with no failure id has no assertion name to report under; tREFI had none, so the refresh-interval assertion reports under a proposed TIMING_012.
rules.discovered_by: sva_rules.json max_interval_rules (tREFI) — no taxonomy id names tREFI

standard.name: JESD79-3 (DDR3)
standard.note: MRS-to-MRS command spacing. Stated in nanoseconds in timing_model (4 x tCK).

rules.question: What is the minimum spacing between consecutive mode-register-set commands (tMRD)?
rules.consequence: The init sequence issues four MRS commands; without tMRD their spacing cannot be asserted, so INIT_002 is only partially checkable.
rules.discovered_by: sva_rules.json command_groups[init] — only tZQinit could be generated

rules.question: What is the minimum delay from a mode-register-set command to the next non-MRS command (tMOD)?
rules.consequence: ZQCL after the last MRS cannot be checked for tMOD without it.
